newsitem.title: USA: Gasoline prices drop on huge rise in U.S. oil stocks.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline prices drop on huge rise in U.S. oil stocks.

text.p: Gasoline prices fell Wednesday after new data suggested that consumption of gasoline and crude oil might be dropping ahead of the peak summer driving season.
Unleaded gasoline for June delivery closed down 0.38 cent at 64.38 a gallon after plunging more than a penny earlier in the session on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Crude oil for June delivery ended 2 cents higher at $21.39 a barrel after recovering from a sell-off of 52 cents.
The American Petroleum Institute, a trade group, reported a large jump of 7 million barrels in crude oil inventories from the previous week and a startling 23 million-barrel year-on-year increase.
The jump in supplies was supported by U.S. Department of Energy's own figures.
"The APIs and DOE (figures) confirmed each other, so you got to believe the data," said Victor Yu, vice-president at Refco Inc. in New York.
The numbers looked equally gloomy for gasoline, the product that traditionally supports oil prices during the northern hemisphere's summer by sucking in imports from abroad.

API statistics showed a much larger than anticipated 6.5-million-barrel rise in gasoline stocks last week, suggesting there will be less import demand during the peak U.S. summer driving season than previously believed.

Oil supplies look set to outstrip demand this summer, with members of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries busting their output quotas, increased non-OPEC production and stagnating demand.
However, oil traders have clutched at straws to mark up prices in the past week, seeing short-term support in Gulf tension and tribal feuds blocking oil movement in Nigeria.
